URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/

# Koshin Studio

  A one-person studio. I build browser games and small apps, and write down what I measure.

  Free. No install, no sign-up.

## Play

- Kaeru Sekai (Returning World) (https://koshinstudio.com/play/kaeru-sekai/) — A 3D world-restoring game: plant seeds of light to bring a gray world back to green, then settle people and watch 100 years go by. Worlds are generated from a number. The few buttons are in Japanese. (About, English) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/kaeru-sekai/)

- Sushi Stack (https://koshinstudio.com/play/sushitsumu/) — A falling-block puzzle: collide matching sushi toppings to grow them, all the way up to the golden sushi tub. Available in 14 languages, opens in your browser language. (About, English) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/sushitsumu/)

- Negaeri Shogi (https://koshinstudio.com/play/negaeri-shogi/) — A 6×6 board game. Pieces you sandwich defect to your side and get promoted, and chains flip many at once. Local, vs AI, and online with ratings. The game is in English and Japanese. (rules, English) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/negaeri-shogi/)

- Draft Party (https://koshinstudio.com/draft/) — A multiplayer draft game: scout fictional rookies by their abilities, draw lots on ties, then watch seasons of stats and standings together. In four languages, including English. (About, English) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/draft-party/)

- Stop at 10 seconds (https://koshinstudio.com/play/stopwatch10/) — Count ten seconds in your head and stop. Best of three; the smaller the error, the stronger you are. No setup, no sign-up. The interface is in Japanese. (About, English) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/stopwatch10/)

- Anime Type Quiz (https://koshinstudio.com/app/shindananime/en/) — 12 questions, 6 axes: your anime type and the one anime that fits you right now. Free, nothing is sent anywhere. In English.

- トレカダッシュ (Toreca Dash) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/) — Lottery, pre-order and restock alerts for trading cards sold in Japan.

- Sushi Stack scores stopped reaching the leaderboard: I changed the game’s numbers and forgot the server’s re-check (twice) (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/rank-verify-mismatch/)

- Japanese Pokémon card & TCG lottery apps compared: Toreca Dash, Toreget, NowPokeca, Pokeka Tracker and Toreca no Chizu (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/tcg-lottery-app-compare/)

## Tools

- Gacha completion calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/) — How many pulls, and how much money, to collect every type?

- Gacha drop rate and pity calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/) — From the drop rate, how many pulls until you get it?

- Lottery win chance calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/) — From the odds and the number of entries, the chance you win at least once.

- TCG booster box price per pack calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/box-price/) — Is a Japanese booster box priced above retail? Converts it to a price per pack.

  All tools → (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/)

- When you cannot watch everything quickly: popular 128 of 427 sets run fast, and the fastest lane yields to the budget (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/hot-lane/)

- Online play that trusts nothing the client says: the server decides moves, clocks and results (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/negaeri-online/)

- Comparing with other sites to count gaps: the first “23% coverage” was a measuring mistake and the truth was 49% (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/coverage-check/)

- I opened the links of displayed articles and compared them: about 60 mistakes, and three mistakes in my own first check (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/destination-check/)

- Four gaps in monitoring X: posts missing from search, accounts that change hands, a store-finding query, and catching up after an outage (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/x-monitoring-gaps/)

- “It gets cleaned up later” hid an entrance bug: 400 near-identical products were re-created every day (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/cleanup-hides-entrance/)

- A secret token was in the logs in plain text: scrub at the one exit that cannot be forgotten (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/secret-in-logs/)

- Moving from Cloud Functions to a ¥4,300 server: ¥3,700 a day, Yahoo! failing in the EEA, and five traps (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/vps-migration/)

- Checks that logged “deferred to next run” had never run: three time budgets counted from the same start (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/budget-starved/)

- “That’s just a Beyblade” came back after I added a gate: the blocked value leaked in another form (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/leaked-value/)

- With no ads, 25 real-device checks were blocked: test ads in developer mode only, and no hard-coded prize names (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/test-ads/)

- I fixed a timeout three times and it did not stop: the culprit was a second process under the same lock (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/timeout-third-fix/)

- Looking up an ambiguous store name returns Shizuoka, the middle of Japan: I judged by Google’s own answer, not a list of chains (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/geocode-shizuoka/)

- A function named “load from iCloud if newer” compared nothing: a 20-record history could become 1 (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/icloud-overwrite/)

- If you throw failure away, the screen lies: a calendar that said “registered” with none added, a frozen OCR, a notification without a store name (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/swallowed-failure/)

- Candidates were found, yet reading the answer failed every time: a URL cut at 200 tokens, and a search that returned 400 on hyphens (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/truncated-answer/)

- “One page = one case” was false: articles of a shop taking 6 products on one form were hidden just for sharing a link (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/one-page-many-cases/)

- “ヤマダ電機” versus “ヤマダデンキ”: spelling variants and duplicates had three overlapping causes (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/store-name-variants/)

- English and katakana names share no characters: a fingerprint gate rejected 42 correct matches (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/transliteration-gate/)

- “Automate everything that can be”: counting showed 66 repair jobs had never run on a schedule, and I added only six (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/automate-sorted/)

- “The server went down and I cannot recover it” was wrong: only inbound SSH had been blocked (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/misdiagnosis-down/)

- “Weird articles keep multiplying”: I counted by creation route and closed the entrances, and my counting was wrong twice (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/weird-articles-by-route/)

- An aggregator crawl read only page 1: card articles were on pages 2–4, and only the first 6,000 characters went to the AI (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/aggregator-pagination/)

- “Not just noticing; not letting it happen”: turning a report-only monitor into one that fills gaps on the spot (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/fill-the-gap/)

- The same report for the third time: a SwiftUI button responded only on its text, and my two earlier “fixes” did nothing (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/swiftui-hit-area/)

# Negaeri Shogi

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/negaeri-shogi/)

  Sandwiched pieces defect to your side.
Defected pieces get promoted.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/negaeri-shogi/)

  Free. Runs in your browser, no install or sign-up. The game is available in English and Japanese.

      The starting position

      Mid-game against the AI

## What it is

  A small 6×6 board and shogi pieces, played like Reversi: drop a piece from your hand so that it sandwiches your opponent’s pieces in a line, and the sandwiched pieces flip to your side. Every piece that flips is also promoted (pawn to tokin, rook to dragon, bishop to horse). A promoted piece moves in new ways, so it can create new sandwiches, and the flips chain. A single move can change the whole board.

## Rules in short

- Four kinds of pieces: king, pawn, rook and bishop. They move as in shogi.

- On your turn you either drop a piece from your hand (this is when sandwiching happens) or move a piece on the board (no flipping).

- Sandwiching works in all 8 directions. The edge of the board also counts as an end, so pieces pushed against the edge can flip together.

- Kings never flip. Pieces next to your own king do not flip either, so the squares around the king are safe.

- Capture the opponent’s king to win. If neither side can move, the player with more pieces wins.

- Online games have 3 minutes per player, plus 5 seconds per move.

## Ways to play

- Two players on one device.

- Against the AI at three levels (weak, medium, strong). The AI runs in your browser.

- Online against another player, with an Elo-style rating and a ranking. A name is stored, and no sign-up is needed.

## About the balance

  The numbers (how many pieces each side holds, the king’s protection) were tuned by AI self-play. Balance in human-versus-human games has not been verified yet. If one side feels too strong, please tell me.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/negaeri-shogi/)

  This is the English version of the Japanese page (https://koshinstudio.com/works/negaeri-shogi/). Online play stores your name, rating and results (see the privacy page (https://koshinstudio.com/privacy/), in Japanese).

# Anime Type Quiz

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/shindananime/)

  12 questions, 6 axes.
Your anime type, and the one anime that fits you right now.

  Start the quiz (free, about 1 minute) (https://koshinstudio.com/app/shindananime/en/)

  Free, runs in your browser, no sign-up. Your answers never leave your device.

## What it is

  The Anime Type Quiz is a free quiz that finds the anime that suits you right now. It asks up to 50 questions about six axes (world, aftertaste, structure, taste, visuals and viewing style), your taste in picture quality and era, and themes such as romance, gore and isekai. Twelve questions are enough to get your six-axis type; the rest are optional. From your answers it works out the direction of each axis and gives you a type code (for example RDCP-VM) and a nickname. There are 64 possible types.

  Unlike most personality quizzes, it does not stop at the type. It then picks, from a database of over 6,000 anime, the one closest to you at the moment.

## It picks real titles

  You get a “destined pick” and two runners-up. Even people with the same type get different titles, because the pick also takes into account the years you prefer and the themes you like or dislike. If you have already seen a title, press “Seen it” and the next best match moves up.

  Closeness between titles is measured by cosine similarity of the six-axis vectors. Popularity and era preferences add only a little, on purpose: if they counted for more, the same few titles would come up for everyone.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many questions, and how long does it take?

  Twelve questions (about 30 seconds) give you your type and your destined pick. If you keep going, up to 50 questions refine the result with era and theme preferences. Every question is multiple choice.

### Are my answers or results stored anywhere?

  No. Your answers are calculated on your device and are not sent anywhere.

### Will the same type always get the same anime?

  No. The pick also reflects the years you prefer and the themes you like or avoid, so it differs from person to person.

### Do I need to install anything?

  No. It works in any browser, on a phone or a computer.

### Where do the data and the English titles come from?

  The database is built from publicly available information about anime and is used only for per-title tendencies; it does not keep review text. English titles and detail links come from AniList. A few titles have no English title yet and show the original Japanese title. Streaming availability differs by country, so the buttons link to JustWatch and other services rather than to a single store.

  Start the quiz (free, about 1 minute) (https://koshinstudio.com/app/shindananime/en/)

  This is the English version of the Japanese page (https://koshinstudio.com/works/shindananime/). The quiz’s questions and result texts are in English at the link above; the Japanese version is at /app/shindananime/ (https://koshinstudio.com/app/shindananime/).

# Toreca Dash (トレカダッシュ)

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/torecadash/)

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/torecadash/)

  Other languages: 日本語 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/torecadash/)

  Lotteries, pre-orders, first-come sales.
The Japanese card drops that are hard to keep up with, in one place, with alerts.

  Open in the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920)

  Free to download. Pro is an optional paid upgrade.

## What it is

  Sales of trading cards in Japan are announced one store at a time, on store sites and on X. By the time you notice, the deadline has passed. Toreca Dash collects announcements from stores and online shops across Japan and takes you straight to the page where you can apply or buy.

## Main features

### Feed

  See open lotteries, pre-orders and first-come sales, filtered by game and sale type.

### Alerts

  Get notified as soon as something new appears for a product or game you follow.

### Deadline calendar

  Lottery deadlines and result dates, day by day, so you do not miss an entry.

### Entry tracker

  Record the lotteries you entered, and the results and purchases.

### Map

  Share in-store stock and lottery information with other users.

## Supported games

  Pokémon Card Game, Yu-Gi-Oh!, ONE PIECE Card Game, Union Arena, Lorcana, Duel Masters, Dragon Ball, Gundam, Magic: The Gathering, Weiss Schwarz, Detective Conan, hololive, Digimon, Haikyu!! Babo-ca!!, Palworld (15 in total).

## Toreca Dash Pro (optional, paid)

- Unlimited product follows, keyword alerts and excluded keywords.

- The fastest alerts for first-come and surprise sales (the free version is about 15 minutes behind).

- Filter to stores near your location.

- Full notification history, entry statistics, calendar export and CSV export.

- Track the value and profit/loss of your collection from purchase records.

- No ads.

## Good to know before you use it

- Store information is mostly in Japanese. Store names, announcements and product names are shown as published in Japan.

- Many Japanese stores require a Japanese address, phone number or store membership to enter a lottery. Check the conditions on each store’s own page before you apply.

- The app shows the information and sends you to the store. It does not buy or enter lotteries for you.

- Screens are available in Japanese and English. More languages are being added.

## Calculators for lotteries and pre-orders

- Lottery win chance calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/) — the chance of winning at least one lottery from the odds and the number of entries.

- Trading-card box and pack unit-price calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/calc/box-price/) (Japanese) — turn a box price into a per-pack price and compare it with the list price.

## FAQ

### Is it free?

  Yes. The main features are free. Pro is an optional paid plan.

### Do I need an account?

  No. The feed, alerts and calendar work without signing in. Sign in with Apple is only used for map posts and the daily fortune.

### Is it an official app?

  No. It is an unofficial app made by an individual, and is not affiliated with any card game publisher or store. Information comes from stores’ public announcements; always confirm the latest details on the store’s official page before you apply or buy.

  Open in the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920)

  Support (https://cardalerthub.web.app/support.html) / Terms (https://cardalerthub.web.app/terms.html) / Privacy (https://cardalerthub.web.app/privacy.html)

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/sushitsumu/

# Sushi Stack

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/sushitsumu/)

  Start with rice and merge matching toppings to grow them.
The final piece is the golden sushi tub.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/sushitsumu/)

  Free. Runs in your browser, no install or sign-up. Available in 14 languages including English.

    On a computer, the score sits to the left of the tub and the ranking to the right

      Title screen

      Playing

      The sushi encyclopedia

    11tiers of toppings
    14languages
    300games verified by auto-play

## What it is

  You drop pieces of rice into a tub from above. When two of the same topping touch, they become the next topping up: rice becomes egg, egg becomes shrimp, shrimp becomes salmon, and so on, up 11 tiers.

  You lose when the tub overflows. It is that simple, but bigger toppings take more room, so stacking without thinking ahead gets you stuck quickly. Each time you choose where to drop, and it adds up.

  When a merge produces a topping that immediately merges again, that is a “chain.” Five in a row is a “big chain,” and the score jumps.

## What is in it

### The sushi encyclopedia

  You can see only the toppings you have made so far; the rest are shown as silhouettes. It is stored per device, so everyone fills it differently. There are 12 kinds in total (including gari, the pickled ginger).

### Ranking (online leaderboard)

  Today’s top and the all-time top. Enter a name and submit to be listed. On a computer, it is always shown at the right of the screen.

### The menu mode

  The chef calls out orders such as “two tuna,” and if you make exactly that within the time you get a bonus. The longer you keep fulfilling orders, the higher the multiplier, and it resets to one when you miss. Scores run about 1.6 times those of normal play, so it has its own ranking.

### Gari

  About once in twenty drops, gari comes instead of a topping. It removes one topping it touches, an escape for when you have stacked badly.

## What you need to play

  Just a browser. No install and no sign-up. On a phone, drag to choose the position and release to drop. On a computer, you can also play with the left and right arrow keys and the space bar.

  It supports 14 languages: Japanese, English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Polish, Turkish, Russian, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Korean and Chinese.

## How it is made

  The whole thing is one HTML file. It uses Matter.js (https://brm.io/matter-js/) for physics, and the sushi is drawn on a Canvas every time rather than shown as images. The ranking runs on Cloudflare Workers and D1, and the server re-verifies the sequence of moves it receives before ranking it.

  The balance was tuned by letting the game play itself and taking numbers first. That story is in the development log (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/anago/).

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/sushitsumu/)

  Development logs for this game

- The conger eel was too big: finding why the last piece was out of reach (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/anago/)

- “The pile settles at 89%” was wrong: my measurement was wrong (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/sushi-measure/)

# Stop at exactly 10 seconds!

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/stopwatch10/)

  Press start and count ten seconds in your head.
When you think it is time, stop.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/stopwatch10/)

  Free. Runs in your browser, no install or sign-up. The screen text is in Japanese, but the game is just a start button and numbers.

      Before starting

      While counting. Nothing moves

      After three attempts

    3attempts per game
    3modes
    1,000one-thousandth of a second

## What it is

  The screen shows no numbers, no ticks and no sound. Between pressing and stopping, nothing moves. All you can rely on is the second hand inside you.

  You stop three times and see your error from the target. Some people are off by 0.5 seconds, and some stop within 0.02. It is shown per attempt rather than as a total, because that makes your skill easier to feel. The best single attempt of the three is also kept. The average is skill; the best single is luck of the day.

## Three modes

### 10 seconds, no hint

  The basic way to play: three attempts. There is no clue at all.

### 10 seconds, with a hint

  A clock is shown for the first 3 seconds only. Match your own beat to it and do the rest by yourself. The moment 3 seconds pass, the display disappears completely.

### 100 seconds, one shot

  One attempt only. While you count the 100 seconds there is nothing to do. If you leave the screen (switch tabs or the screen turns off), that attempt becomes invalid.

## Why three decimals

  Browser clocks differ in coarseness by device. performance.now() is deliberately made less precise as a Spectre countermeasure: Chrome in 5 µs steps, Safari and Firefox in 1 ms steps.

  If six decimals were shown, a device with a coarser clock would more often end in 000 and gain an advantage. In a game about being “exact,” the luck of your device would decide the ranking. So I cut at three decimals to put every device on the same ground.

## Nothing moving

  While building it, I once put a blinking lamp somewhere in the display. It became a stand-in metronome. If something flashes at 1 Hz in your sight, people can count along with it, and a game about counting by yourself vanishes entirely.

  Now there is nothing that moves periodically during measurement: no pulsing buttons, no blinking, no animation. From the moment you press until you stop, the screen is completely still.

## How it is made

  The whole thing is one HTML file with zero external libraries. The digits are drawn as SVG polygons in a seven-segment shape, so it depends on no font either. The sound effects use no audio files and are generated on the spot.

  The stop time is taken from event.timeStamp of pointerdown, because waiting for click adds extra delay. Your records stay in your device, per mode.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/stopwatch10/)

  Development log for this game

- Making a 10-second stopwatch ranking fair: 3 decimals, ties and write counts (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/stopwatch-rank/)

  This is the English version of the Japanese page (https://koshinstudio.com/works/stopwatch10/).

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/draft-party/

# Draft Party

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/draft-party/)

  Scout rookies by their abilities. Tie with someone? Lottery!
A draft day for everyone, in your browser.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/draft/)

  Free. Runs in your browser, no install or sign-up. Available in Japanese, English, Korean and Traditional Chinese.

    12teams at most
    2modes
    4languages

## What it is

  Name your team and pick fictional rookies. In Round 1 everyone bids at the same time, hidden from the others, and all bids are revealed together. If teams chose the same player, they draw lots: the competing teams take turns picking one hidden paper, and when everyone has picked, all papers open at once. Only the winner gets the rights; the others re-bid on a different player.

  From Round 2, teams pick one at a time, and the order flips every round. At the end, the contract talks are announced — “signed” or “refused”. You can turn your result into an image and share it on X.

  Looking for a draft game or a draft simulator? The flow and rules are laid out on their own pages: Baseball draft simulator (https://koshinstudio.com/draft/en/simulator/).

## Two modes

### Scout mode

  First, each participant raises their own player through three years of high school. Form and luck change the results, and training the same stat repeatedly can unlock special skills. The raised players join everyone else’s and the CPU’s in the draft (yours can be drafted by you only in the final round, if it is still there), and when one is picked, its owner decides whether to sign or refuse.

  Pick fictional rookies by their abilities, potential and records. The abilities are the scouts’ estimates and can differ from reality. Signed players grow over several years while every team plays every other team. You get yearly standings, head-to-head records against every team, titles such as batting champion and wins leader, Rookie of the Year and draft grades — revealed to everyone at the same time, so you can react together with stamps and chat. The host can also register the players.

### Choice mode

  Pick from a list the host prepared — for example, everyone in your class or 50 favorite anime. Great for groups of friends.

## After the draft: careers and the world ranking

  When the draft ends you can read how each drafted player’s life turned out: a breakout rookie year, a climb up from the minors, a trade, a comeback after being released, a move overseas, and finally retirement. You see each team’s headline pick first, and can open everyone’s. The events and endings you find collect in a “career log”.

  Players eyeing the majors may refuse to sign, and an “omen” can appear before the result is announced — though sometimes they sign anyway.

  Your draft becomes a Draft Score (the CPU teams’ average is 50) and enters the world ranking (https://koshinstudio.com/draft/ranking) (today, this week, all time). Rooms with the standard settings (12 teams, 6 rounds) count; “multiplayer” (two or more humans) and “solo” are separate boards. You can share the result on X as an image card.

## With friends, or with strangers

- Friends room: enter with a 6-character room code or a link. The host freely chooses the number of teams, rounds, time limit, refusals and mode, and nothing starts until the host presses Start. A public room is listed so strangers can join. The host can also remove anyone who causes trouble.

- Find an open room: browse public rooms and see their rules (teams, rounds, time limit, refusals) before you join.

- Quick join: don’t want to search? One tap puts you in an open room, or starts one with CPU teams so there is no wait.

  Every team gets an original emblem automatically (you can pick another), and you can use your own image in any room (inappropriate images are hidden after reports).

## How it is built

  The server (Cloudflare Workers with Durable Objects) runs all the progress and judging. Round 1 bids are not sent to anyone until the reveal, and the winning paper of a lottery is known only to the server until everyone has drawn. Even the host cannot peek at bids or rig a lottery. There is no login, and the sound effects and music are generated in the browser (no audio files).

  The players in Scout mode are fictional people generated at random each time. They have no connection to real players, teams or results, and this game has no connection to any professional league or team.

## What is stored

  For the sake of play inside a room, a device-generated number, your team name, what you pick, chat messages and the room settings are kept only for the life of that room, and are all deleted 10 minutes after the game ends. The world ranking records only your team name, Draft Score, grade (S–D) and date when a game ends (no device number and no chat). When you share an image card on X, the shared result image and its text are kept on the server for 7 days. Details are on the privacy page (https://koshinstudio.com/en/privacy/).

    Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/draft/)

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/kaeru-sekai/

# Kaeru Sekai (Returning World)

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/works/kaeru-sekai/)

  Plant seeds of light in a world that has lost its color.
When the green returns, let people settle and watch 100 years go by.

  Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/kaeru-sekai/)

  Free. Runs in your browser on phones and computers, no install or sign-up. The few buttons are labeled in Japanese, but the game is played by tapping the ground and looking around. “Kaeru Sekai” (還る世界) means “the world that returns.”

      Green returns from where a seed lands

      Days and nights pass while people settle

      You can walk right into the houses

    10seeds of light
    100years to watch
    300people, roughly, before it tips

## How it plays

  The first view is gray: grass and trees have withered. Tap the ground and a seed of light falls, and green spreads from there. You have 10 seeds. Where you plant them changes how fast the world recovers. Even after the seeds run out, the edge of the green keeps creeping outward.

  When the green is back, you choose how many people will live there. With few, houses and fields multiply, roads connect, and in time a church or a tower rises in the middle of the village. At night the windows light up. With too many, the green is worn away and the land turns gray again. How many it can hold is for you to find out.

## A world from a number

  Each world is generated from a number between 1 and 99,999: valleys, meadows, fjords, deserts, islands, volcanoes, archipelagos and snowfields. The same number always makes the same world, for anyone. Send a link with the number and a friend can play the same world. If you pick nothing, you get the world of the day.

  Sometimes you land on a rare one: a world in full cherry blossom, a world with a strange sky, a single rock spire piercing the clouds, a huge caldera, a land of lakes. Houses follow the land too: red wooden houses of the north, white walls with blue domes, sun-dried brick.

## Walk, and take photos

  Press “walk” (歩く) to walk through the world in first person. On a phone, the left side of the screen moves and the right side looks around. On a computer, WASD moves and dragging looks around. Grass sways in the wind underfoot, and people come and go in the village.

  Get close to a house and you can go inside: a fire in the hearth, a dining table, jars on a shelf. Each house has a different number of people living in it. Press the shutter to keep the scene as a photo.

## How it is made

  Everything is computed and drawn on the spot. The terrain is built from layered noise, with mountains, inlets, dunes, plateaus and craters shaped differently for each kind of world. Each pixel of the ground gets its color from height, slope and how far the green has returned. The sky is computed from atmospheric scattering, clouds drift, and water reflects its surroundings.

  So that it runs on phones, the level of detail drops automatically depending on the device’s speed. If it feels heavy at first, wait a moment and it gets lighter.

    Play now (https://koshinstudio.com/play/kaeru-sekai/)

# Tools

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/calc/)

  Calculators

  These calculators run only in your browser. The numbers you enter are not sent anywhere. Each one is checked against the results of a computer simulation of 200,000 players.

  Each shows not only the average but also how long an unlucky player takes (the number of tries by which 90% and 99% of people succeed). Looking only at the average makes it easy to believe “it should hit by then.” If you are not sure which to use:

- You want every type (capsule toys, randomly packed collections) → the completion calculator.

- You want one specific item (a gacha with a fixed drop rate, with or without pity) → the drop rate and pity calculator.

- You want to know whether a booster box is priced above retail → the price per pack calculator.

- You enter several lottery sales (with known or estimated odds) → the lottery win chance calculator.

  All of these are probabilities, not guarantees. Where the assumptions do not hold (odds that change mid-game, lotteries that forbid multiple entries), each page explains it under “when this calculation does not fit.”

- Calculator
      Gacha completion calculatorHow many pulls, and how much money, to collect every type. The average, the pulls by which 90% of people finish, and whether a complete set is cheaper. (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/)

- Calculator
      Gacha drop rate and pity calculatorFrom the drop rate, how many pulls until you get it. Supports how many copies you want and a pity (guaranteed after N pulls). (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/)

- Calculator
      TCG booster box price per pack calculatorTurn a booster box or set price into a price per pack and compare it with the list price. Typical pack counts per box for each game, counted from 179 listings. (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/box-price/)

- Calculator
      Lottery win chance calculatorFrom the odds and the number of entries, the chance you win at least once. Works even when each entry has different odds. (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/)

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/

# Gacha completion calculator

  How many pulls, and how much money, to collect every type?

  Enter the number of types and how many you already own. You get the average number of pulls, the number of pulls within which 90% of people finish, the cost, and whether a complete set is cheaper.

## How it works

  If you own c types, one pull gives a new type with probability (n − c) / n. The average is n × (1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + …). The “90% of people” number is found by stepping one pull at a time until the chance of being done passes 90%. For 5 types, simulating 200,000 people gave the same numbers (average 11.41, half within 10, 90% within 18, 99% within 28).

## When this does not apply

- It assumes every pull gives each type with the same probability. If some types are rarer (like a secret), completing takes more pulls than shown.

- Machines with a fixed set of capsules inside have fewer duplicates. They are not supported.

- This is a probability calculation. It does not mean you will complete the collection.

  For a single item or a pity (guaranteed after N pulls), use the drop rate and pity calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/).


---

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/

# Gacha drop rate and pity calculator

  From the drop rate, how many pulls until you get it?

  Enter the drop rate (%). You get how many pulls it takes: the average, and the numbers within which 50%, 90% and 99% of people succeed. It also supports how many you want and a pity (guaranteed on the N-th pull).

## How it works

  Without a pity, the number of pulls until the first success follows a geometric distribution with probability p; for k copies the average is k ÷ p. With a pity at N, the N-th pull is guaranteed and the count restarts after a hit. A drop rate of 3% does not mean “guaranteed within 33 pulls”: after 100 pulls about 5% of people still have nothing.

## When this does not apply

- Use the published rate as it is. The calculator cannot know whether the published rate is accurate.

- It assumes each pull is independent. Games whose rate rises as you pull (soft pity) are not supported.

- Pity here means “guaranteed on pull N, then the count restarts.” Exchange systems and carry-over pity are not included.

  To collect every type, use the completion calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/).

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/box-price/

# TCG booster box price per pack calculator

  How much per pack? How many times the list price?

  This converts the price of a booster box or set into a price per pack and compares it with the list price. In Japan, trading card list prices are usually given per pack, but what is sold is often a box (a case holding several packs) or a set. Comparing a box price directly with the per-pack list price makes a fair price look like a “30× scalper price.” This calculator puts both in the same unit first.

  Amounts are in Japanese yen, as cards are priced in Japan. The calculation itself works in any currency if you enter every amount in the same one.

  The typical counts are for a standard Japanese booster box. Products differ, so always enter the pack count printed on the product page or the box.

## Example 1: is a ¥5,782 ONE PIECE box a scalper price?

  ONE PIECE Card Game booster boxes in Japan always hold 24 packs. With a list price of ¥240 per pack, the box list price is ¥240 × 24 = ¥5,760. A listing at ¥5,782 is only ¥22 above that: essentially list price. Compared directly with ¥240 per pack, it looks like a 24× markup. This exact mistake was reported as a “scalper price” while I was developing my app, and it turned out to be a false alarm.

## Example 2: the Pokémon box that looked “30×”

  A Japanese Pokémon Card Game expansion booster box holds 30 packs at a list price of ¥180 per pack, so the box list price is ¥180 × 30 = ¥5,400. Sold at exactly ¥5,400, it is still 30 times the per-pack price. For a while my app had learned the pack count for not a single Pokémon expansion box, so it compared ¥5,400 with ¥180 and showed a “30× scalper price.”

  Pack counts differ by product, though. The Pokémon “30th CELEBRATION” box holds 20 packs at ¥360 each, for a list price of ¥7,200. Assuming “Pokémon means 30 packs” makes the opposite mistake.

## How many packs are in a box: counted from 179 listings

  While building the app, I took the 480 box listings in its feed and counted the 179 whose titles stated a pack count. By game:

    Game | Typical packs | What I counted

      Magic: The Gathering | 30 | 60 listings (33 with 30 packs, 19 with 12)

      Weiß Schwarz | 12 | 45 listings (25 with 10 packs, 17 with 12)

      Yu-Gi-Oh! OCG | 30 | 19 listings (12 with 15 packs, 6 with 30)

      Duel Masters | 16 | 14 listings (6 with 16 packs, 4 with 14)

      Digimon Card Game | 24 | 14 listings, all 24 packs

      Gundam Card Game | 24 | 8 listings, all 24 packs

      hololive OFFICIAL CARD GAME | 12 | 8 listings, all 12 packs

      ONE PIECE Card Game | 24 | 5 of 6 listings with 24 packs (said to be standardized officially)

      Haikyu!! VABACA!! BREAK | 18 | Both listings 18 packs

      Union Arena | 16 | The official product page states 16 packs

      Pokémon Card Game | 30 | Expansion boxes hold 30 packs (with exceptions)

  Three cautions when reading this table:

- These are counts from listing titles, not official figures. Some games are standardized officially, like ONE PIECE; others split into two values (MTG play and collector boxes, Yu-Gi-Oh! 15 and 30). Where a game splits, the typical value is the larger one.

- Not a single box held 40 packs. The largest I counted was 36.

- Do not read a bundle such as a “5-pack set” as a box’s contents. It underestimates the box list price and makes normal listings look like scalping.

## How to use it

- Check the pack count on the product page or box and enter it under “Packs inside.”

- Look up the list price per pack in the official announcement (the publisher’s site) and enter it.

- If there is shipping, enter it under “Shipping and other costs.” Comparing with shipping included is closer to what you actually pay.

- Read “how many times the list price” and “difference from the list price total.”

## When this calculation does not fit

- Some products announce a box price rather than a per-pack price. Then enter 1 for “Packs inside” and the box list price as the per-pack price.

- If a product includes a bonus (such as a promo card), its value is not part of this calculation.

- For popular products, market prices differing from list price is normal. This calculator only shows “how many times the list price.” It does not decide whether a price is fair. Unpopular products selling below list price is normal too.

  For the chance of winning when you enter lotteries, use the lottery win chance calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/). To follow lotteries at Japanese stores, see the comparison of Japanese TCG lottery apps (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/tcg-lottery-app-compare/).

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/

# Lottery win chance calculator

    How many entries until you win?

  If you enter several lotteries, what is the chance that you win at least one? Enter the odds (for example “1 in 5”) or the win chance (%). If each lottery has different odds, list them in “Win chance per entry” separated by commas and the calculator combines them. Trading-card stores in Japan often sell hot items by lottery, which is why this exists; it works for any lottery.

  If you enter odds, they take priority over the win chance field (chance = 100 ÷ odds). If you fill in “Win chance per entry”, the odds, chance and entries fields are ignored.

## Example: five lotteries at 1 in 5

- Each entry has a 20% chance (1 ÷ 5). The chance that all five lose is 0.8 to the 5th power, 32.8%. So the chance of at least one win is 67.2%.

- The average number of wins is 5 × 20% = 1.0. But exactly 1 win happens only 41.0% of the time; 2 or more is 26.3% and 3 or more is 5.8%.

- “I entered five 1-in-5 lotteries, so I should win one” is not true. About one person in three loses all five.

## Quick table: chance of at least one win

  Same odds on every entry, each result independent of the others.

    Odds (win chance) | 1 entry | 3 | 5 | 10 | 20

      1 in 2 (50%) | 50.0% | 87.5% | 96.9% | 99.9% | 99.99%+

      1 in 3 (33.3%) | 33.3% | 70.4% | 86.8% | 98.3% | 99.97%

      1 in 5 (20%) | 20.0% | 48.8% | 67.2% | 89.3% | 98.8%

      1 in 10 (10%) | 10.0% | 27.1% | 41.0% | 65.1% | 87.8%

      1 in 20 (5%) | 5.0% | 14.3% | 22.6% | 40.1% | 64.2%

      1 in 50 (2%) | 2.0% | 5.9% | 9.6% | 18.3% | 33.2%

  Ten entries at 1 in 10 give 65.1% for at least one win, so about one person in three (34.9%) wins nothing. Doubling the entries does not double the chance (1 in 10: 41.0% with 5 entries, 65.1% with 10).

## Quick table: entries needed

    Odds (win chance) | Half win | 90% win | 99% win

      1 in 2 (50%) | 1 entry | 4 entries | 7 entries

      1 in 3 (33.3%) | 2 entries | 6 entries | 12 entries

      1 in 5 (20%) | 4 entries | 11 entries | 21 entries

      1 in 10 (10%) | 7 entries | 22 entries | 44 entries

      1 in 20 (5%) | 14 entries | 45 entries | 90 entries

      1 in 50 (2%) | 35 entries | 114 entries | 228 entries

  The entries needed for 90% grow roughly in proportion to the odds (22 at 1 in 10, 45 at 1 in 20).

## How it works

- No win at all: multiply the chance of losing (1 − win chance) for every entry. At least one win is 1 minus that. With equal chances it is 1 − (1 − p)n.

- Distribution of wins: entries are added one at a time, updating “exactly j wins” (a Poisson binomial distribution). It works when chances differ per entry.

- Entries needed: the smallest n with n ≥ ln(1 − q) ÷ ln(1 − p).

  I checked the maths a second way. For equal chances (20% five times, 8% ten times) and for different chances (10%, 30%, 5%, 50%), I simulated 200,000 runs each and compared “exactly j wins” with this calculator. Every value was within 0.2 percentage points, which is the noise of 200,000 trials.

## When this does not apply

- You supply the win chance. Stores rarely publish the number of applicants, so “odds” are an estimate. The calculator cannot tell if your number is right.

- Each entry is independent. If a lottery bans duplicate entries, or favours members or past buyers, the real chance differs from these numbers.

- You meet the entry rules. One entry per person, ID checks, purchase limits and pickup locations are set by each store. Entering under multiple names or accounts is often against the rules.

- This is probability, not a promise. Do not buy things you do not want just to raise your number of entries.

  For gacha, see the gacha rate and pity calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/) and the complete-the-set calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/).


---

URL: https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/rank-verify-mismatch/

# Sushi Stack scores stopped reaching the leaderboard: I changed the game’s numbers and forgot the server’s re-check (twice)

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/rank-verify-mismatch/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-11-07
Development log of Sushi Stack / October 2026

  My browser game Sushi Stack (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/sushitsumu/) has an online leaderboard. At some point, runs that were played normally to the end stopped appearing on it. The screen said: “Your record did not add up, so it could not be posted.” The cause was that I had changed numbers in the game and not updated the same numbers in the server’s re-check. And after I thought I had fixed it, a second mismatch was still there.

  This article is written from the work on October 23, 2026 and from the commits in the repository.

## What the leaderboard re-check does

  A leaderboard anyone can post to attracts fake scores. So the game sends the sequence of play (when, what was dropped, what merged) together with the score, and the server recounts the score and refuses it if it does not match the claim (server/verify.js).

  It does not replay the physics (how the toppings rolled). That does not fit in the free tier’s CPU time (10 ms per call). Instead it checks only that the books balance:

- Drop sequence: the toppings dropped match the sequence regenerated from the seed

- Inventory: nothing merged without two of the same topping existing

- Score: adding up the recorded events gives the claimed score

- Timing: drop intervals, chain parents and order contents are within the rules

  The weakness of this design: if even one number differs between the game and the server, honest records get rejected too.

## Mismatch 1: the golden-tub bonus was still 8,000

  On September 10 I tuned the length of a run and its rewards so that a “double golden tub” (making two golden tubs and merging them) became reachable. As part of that I raised the bonus for merging two golden tubs (GOLDEN_BONUS) from 8,000 to 25,000 (commit 174bb2b). The re-check still used 8,000.

     | Game (index.html) | Re-check (verify.js)

      Merging two golden tubs | +25,000 | +8,000

  Any run that merged two golden tubs got 25,000 from the game and 8,000 from the server, so it always disagreed. Only the very best runs, the ones that reached the double golden tub, were kept off the board. I fixed this (commit 2753293) and deployed the leaderboard server.

## Mismatch 2: the falling toppings were still 3 kinds

  After the fix, I got a report: “A normal run that ended quickly was not posted either.” That run never reached a golden tub. The first mismatch could not explain it.

  Looking further, a commit on the same September 10 (6ebabc3) had increased the falling toppings from 3 kinds to 5: rice, egg and shrimp, plus salmon and tuna, drawn with weights (ROLL_W = [1, 1, 2, 3, 2]). The re-check still “drew from 3 kinds with equal probability.”

     | Game | Re-check

      Kinds of topping | 5 (weighted) | 3 (equal)

      How each drop is drawn | One random number, subtract weights until it runs out | One random number × 3, rounded down

  The sequence regenerated from the seed drifts almost every time, and the first drifted drop is rejected as “sequence does not match.” In other words, since September 10, almost every normal run should have been rejected, golden tub or not. The golden-tub bug was a second mismatch hiding behind the main one.

  I cannot count how many players were affected. The server code had no counter for rejected records.

## It happened despite a warning comment

  From the very beginning, the top of verify.js said:

> The constants here must equal the ones in index.html. Touching only one side rejects honest records, so always change both.

  The warning was there. Still, in about 30 minutes on September 10 (14:05 to 14:34), I stacked five tuning commits on the game, and none of them touched the re-check. Writing it down does not keep it true. So I assumed it would be broken again and made a machine watch it.

  tools/verify-sync.mjs checks two things:

- The scoring constants (merge points, golden-tub bonus, chain cap, drop interval and so on) and formulas (chain multiplier, order rewards) are the same in the game and the re-check

- Given the same 6 seeds, the game’s rollItem() and the re-check’s makeRoller() each produce 2,000 drops, and the sequences match

  Run against the code before the fix, it caught both the golden-tub bonus and the sequence mismatch (all 6 seeds). After the fix, all 12,000 drops matched. It also runs first in the combined check (tools/check.mjs).

  A test that only compares constants would not have found the second mismatch (the weights). It was not a number that changed but the way of drawing itself. Only a test that actually runs both sides and compares their output caught it.

## Confirming with the real game

  A passing comparison does not prove that records the game really produces will pass. So I used my balance tool (it fast-forwards the game on a virtual clock and lets a bot play) and fed records written by the actual game into the re-check.

    Mode | Runs | Re-check | Score range

      Free play | 4 | All 4 passed | 36,368 – 54,836

      Orders | 4 | All 4 passed | 81,857 – 166,105

  All 8 matched, down to the recounted score. Then I deployed the leaderboard server again and played the live game myself to confirm the score was posted.

  None of the 8 bot runs reached a double golden tub. The path through merging two golden tubs is confirmed only by comparing constants, not by a real record.

## What I learned

- If the same number lives in two places, changing one breaks the other. A comment was not enough.

- “Fixed” may mean only one cause is fixed. Before saying it was fixed, I should have checked that the reported symptom (not posted even without a golden tub) was explained by the cause I fixed.

- I was not counting rejections. I do not know how many people hit this because the server rejected silently. Next, I want to count rejections by reason (sequence, score and so on) so a rise is noticed.

- Turn comparison tests into tests that run both sides. Matching numbers could not catch a change in how values are drawn.

  Related: halving the leaderboard’s free-tier usage (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/ranking-free-tier/) and making the 10-second game’s ranking fair (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/stopwatch-rank/).

  This is the English version of the original Japanese article (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/rank-verify-mismatch/).

# Japanese Pokémon card & TCG lottery apps compared: Toreca Dash, Toreget, NowPokeca, Pokeka Tracker and Toreca no Chizu

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/tcg-lottery-app-compare/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-11-07
Toreca Dash / Comparison / October 2026

  In Japan, new Pokémon Card Game boxes and other popular trading cards are often sold by lottery (抽選, chūsen): you enter at a store or online shop before a deadline, and only winners can buy. Several apps and sites track these lotteries, pre-orders and restocks. This article puts Toreca Dash and four others side by side on the same items, for anyone looking for a Japanese TCG lottery app.

  Disclosure first: I (Koshin) am the developer of Toreca Dash. This is not a neutral third-party comparison. For the other services I wrote only what their official pages and App Store pages said when I checked on October 23, 2026, and marked anything not stated as “not stated.” I also wrote Toreca Dash’s weak points.

  For readers outside Japan: all five services cover stores in Japan, and their information is mostly in Japanese. Most lotteries require a Japanese address or in-store pickup, and some stores require a membership. They are most useful if you live in Japan, are visiting, or use a proxy-buying service.

  See Toreca Dash on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920)

  Toreca Dash on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920 (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920) (free, iPhone) / about page on this site: Toreca Dash (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/)

## Short answer: which one to pick

- You follow games other than Pokémon (Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Gundam and more) or want iPhone push alerts → Toreca Dash (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920) (15 games)

- A browser or LINE is enough, not an iPhone app → Toreget (web and LINE, 6 games)

- Only Pokémon cards, and you want to try free restock alerts first → NowPokeca

- You want to track Pokémon card prices and the profit or loss of your collection → Pokeka Tracker

- You want to find card shops nearby → Toreca no Chizu (lottery listings and alerts: not stated)

  You can combine them, for example Toreca Dash for lottery alerts and another app for prices.

## The five, compared

     | Toreca Dash | Toreget | NowPokeca | Pokeka Tracker | Toreca no Chizu

      Where | App Store (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/id6788758920) | cardchusen.com (https://cardchusen.com/) | App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/-/id6469001897) | App Store (https://apps.apple.com/es/app/pokeka-tracker-%E3%83%9D%E3%82%B1%E3%82%AB%E4%BE%A1%E6%A0%BC%E3%82%92%E7%A2%BA%E8%AA%8D%E3%81%A7%E3%81%8D%E3%82%8B%E3%82%A2%E3%83%97%E3%83%AA/id6450254728) | torecamap.co.jp (https://torecamap.co.jp/)

      Form | iPhone app | Website + LINE alerts | iPhone app | iPhone / iPad app | Website

      Games | 15 (Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Union Arena, Lorcana, Duel Masters, Dragon Ball, Gundam, MTG, Weiß Schwarz, Detective Conan, hololive, Digimon, Haikyu!! VABACA, Palworld) | 6 (Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Pokémon, One Piece, Weiß Schwarz, Duel Masters) | Pokémon (from its name and description) | Pokémon, One Piece | Seen on the page: One Piece, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Pokémon

      Lottery / pre-order list | Yes | Yes (by deadline) | Yes | Lottery alerts | Not stated

      Alerts | Push | LINE | Push (per store) | Push | Not stated

      Store locations on a map | Yes (stores with open lotteries on a map) | No map stated (filter by prefecture) | Not stated | Not stated | Yes (a shop finder; no lottery info stated)

      Deadline calendar / entry log | Yes | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated

      Price / profit tracking | Yes (Pro) | Not stated | Charts for favorite cards | Yes (the core feature) | Market prices listed

      Price | Free + in-app purchase (Pro: ¥480/month, ¥3,800/year, ¥9,800 lifetime) | Not stated | Free + paid ad removal | Free + Pro (Spanish store: €5.99/month, €59.99/year; Japanese price not stated) | No user pricing stated

  Sources: each service’s official page and App Store page, checked on October 23, 2026. Services change, so check the official page before you rely on them.

## Toreca Dash: strengths

### 1. It covers 15 card games

  Pokémon Card Game, Yu-Gi-Oh!, ONE PIECE Card Game, Union Arena, Lorcana, Duel Masters, Dragon Ball, Gundam, Magic: The Gathering, Weiß Schwarz, Detective Conan, hololive, Digimon, Haikyu!! VABACA and Palworld. Among the four I looked at, none published more games. If you collect several games, you do not need separate apps.

Genre filters with counts. Scroll down for all 15

### 2. A map of stores running lotteries now

  The app’s map tab has a mode for stores with open lotteries. It shows a pin for each store that currently accepts lottery or pre-order entries; tapping a pin opens that store’s lottery article.

- Entries past their deadline, or not yet open, are not shown on the map (the code says so).

- Only stores whose location could be determined are pinned. Others appear only in the feed.

- In “sightings” on the same screen, users can post restocks and lotteries they saw in a store. Posts disappear after 12 hours.

  Among the services I checked, I found no other that shows “where lotteries are open right now” on a map (Toreca no Chizu is a shop finder, with no lottery listings stated).

Stores with open lotteries. The number on a pin is how many entries are open thereTap a pin for that store’s lotteries and deadlines, with directions

### 3. No sign-in needed

  The feed, alerts and calendar work without signing in. Sign in with Apple is needed only to post on the map and for the daily fortune.

### 4. Deadline calendar and entry log

  A lottery does not end when you enter: there is a results date and a purchase deadline. The app lays out deadlines on a calendar and lets you record the results of lotteries you entered, so you do not forget whether you applied.

### 5. Many sources

  A server automatically collects official sites, online shops, aggregator sites and public posts on X. What it collects and how much, including the failures, is in the article on crawling aggregator sites (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/aggregator-pagination/) and the article on a crawl returning zero results (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/blocked-page/).

## Toreca Dash: weaknesses

- iPhone only. I distribute only the iPhone version on the App Store. There is no browser or Android version. It needs iOS 17.2 or later.

- On the free plan, first-come and surprise-sale alerts arrive about 15 minutes late. Getting them fastest needs Pro (paid): ¥480/month, ¥3,800/year or ¥9,800 lifetime (as shown on the App Store).

- It shows ads. Removing them takes a ¥480 one-time purchase or Pro.

- Few ratings yet. The App Store rating is 5.0, but from 2 ratings. That tells you little.

- Dedicated apps go deeper on prices. Toreca Dash has collection and profit tracking (Pro), but it does not match an app built around prices, such as Pokeka Tracker.

- Only public information. Lotteries shown only to a store’s members, or announced only to LINE friends, can be missed. Always check the store’s official page before entering.

- It is an unofficial app by an individual developer, not affiliated with any card game’s rights holders or with the stores.

## Toreget

  Official site (cardchusen.com) (https://cardchusen.com/)

  A website that gathers card lottery, pre-order, stock and restock information. Its official page lists 6 games: Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Pokémon, One Piece, Weiß Schwarz and Duel Masters. Alerts go through LINE, with daily lottery reminders. You can filter by prefecture and browse a list of stores.

  Good for people who do not want to install an app, Android users, and anyone who prefers LINE alerts. Points to note: no app is mentioned, and no map is mentioned. Pricing was not stated.

  The operating company also publishes surveys of lottery win rates (for example a September 2026 press release comparing win rates between stores). Win-rate statistics look like Toreget’s strength.

## NowPokeca

  App Store page (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/-/id6469001897)

  An iPhone app that watches Pokémon card sales and sends a push alert when an online shop starts selling (or taking pre-orders). It has a list of lottery sales and per-store alert settings. Free; removing ads is paid ($1.99 on the US store).

  Good for people who only follow Pokémon cards and want to start free. Points to note: it is Pokémon-focused, with no other games mentioned. It had one App Store rating and is made by an individual developer.

## Pokeka Tracker

  App Store page (https://apps.apple.com/es/app/pokeka-tracker-%E3%83%9D%E3%82%B1%E3%82%AB%E4%BE%A1%E6%A0%BC%E3%82%92%E7%A2%BA%E8%AA%8D%E3%81%A7%E3%81%8D%E3%82%8B%E3%82%A2%E3%83%97%E3%83%AA/id6450254728)

  An app centered on Pokémon card prices: daily price updates, PSA 10 and PSA 9 prices, unrealized profit or loss from what you paid, price alerts and lottery alerts, card scanning, and widgets. It also covers One Piece card prices.

  Good for people who want to track the value and profit of their collection. Points to note: Pro looks relatively expensive (what I could confirm was the Spanish store: €5.99/month, €59.99/year; I could not confirm the Japanese price). It needs iOS 18.0 or later.

## Toreca no Chizu (trading card map)

  Official site (torecamap.co.jp) (https://torecamap.co.jp/)

  A web portal for finding trading card shops nearby, with stock search, market prices and tournament information. You pick an area on a map and filter by “open now,” “buys cards,” “parking,” “duel space” and more. I could not find lottery listings or alerts on the page (its columns do explain how individual stores run lotteries).

  Good for finding card shops themselves. To follow lotteries, you would combine it with another service.

## FAQ

### Which shows the most TCG lottery information in one place?

  By number of games, Toreca Dash with 15 was the most among those I checked. For Pokémon only, every service covers it. Choose by your device (iPhone or not) and how you want alerts (an app or LINE).

### Is there a free app for Pokémon card lottery alerts in Japan?

  Toreca Dash (on the free plan, first-come alerts are about 15 minutes late), NowPokeca (free) and Toreget (LINE; pricing not stated) all seemed usable for free. What is free can change.

### Can I find stores running lotteries on a map?

  Yes, in Toreca Dash’s map tab, in the open-lotteries mode. To just find card shops, Toreca no Chizu works.

### Do they cover Yu-Gi-Oh! and One Piece lotteries?

  Toreca Dash (15 games) and Toreget (6 games) both do. NowPokeca is for Pokémon.

### Is anything available on Android?

  Toreget is a website, so it works in any browser. Toreca Dash is iPhone only.

### How can I raise my chance of winning?

  No app changes the win rate itself. What an app can do is reduce missed deadlines and increase the number of stores you enter. One survey found large differences in win rates between stores (Toreget’s data). From the odds and the number of entries, the chance of winning at least once can be computed with the lottery win chance calculator (https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/).

## How I checked, and the limits of this article

- Checked on October 23, 2026. I opened each official page and App Store page and wrote down what they said. I did not use each service to measure alert speed or misses.

- “Not found among those I checked” does not mean “does not exist.” There are other apps and sites for card lotteries.

- Toreca Dash details come from its app description, its code and its App Store page.

- If you spot a mistake, please tell me via the contact page (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#contact). I will check and fix it.

# An aggregator crawl read only page 1: card articles were on pages 2–4, and only the first 6,000 characters went to the AI

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/aggregator-pagination/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-10-17
Development log of the Toreca Dash app / August 2026

  One of my app Toreca Dash’s sources is an aggregator site for stock information, which lists lottery articles together. This crawl had two causes of “things that should appear but did not”.

  Written from my work log of 28 August 2026.

## Cause 1: only the first page of the list was read

  The function that reads the aggregator’s list of lottery articles (fetchNyukaNowChusenArticles) read only page 1. The 11 items on page 1 were mostly game consoles, a virtual pet and plush toys. The trading-card articles were on later pages.

    Kind of article | Where it was

      Pokémon cards | a later page

      Gundam card game | page 2

      Dragon Ball, Digimon, Duel Masters | page 3

      Union Arena, Weiss Schwarz | page 4

  Many existing articles derive from one Pokémon-card roundup, yet the crawl no longer read that article itself. The fix was to follow up to 12 pages.

## Cause 2: only the first 6,000 characters of the body went to the AI

  A Pokémon-card roundup lists 15 or more stores on one page. I gave the AI only the first 6,000 characters of the body, so the later stores dropped out entirely. That is also why the number readable per run wobbled 48, 39, 40.

  The fix was to read all of it in 5,000-character pieces with a 600-character overlap. The import itself uses the same function.

## Found the same day: dates with no year

  The aggregator’s table writes only “30 August (Sun)”. I was not giving the AI today’s date, so Pokémon-card items came back as 30 August 2020. A past deadline is rejected by the entrance gate, so Pokémon-card items from this route were not imported at all. After I put today’s date and “do not fill in a year before today” in the prompt, the open items I could read went from 0 to 46. (This is also told in another article (https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/silent-discard/).)

## What I learned

> Three cut points in an import: pages, characters, years.

- Read a list to its last page. What you want is not necessarily on page 1.

- Check that the AI’s character limit is not dropping the back half. A wobbling count is a sign.

- Pass the whole text, in order, with overlap. If you pass only the head, the rest drops.

- For dates with no year, give today’s date. Otherwise it fills in six years ago.

- “Not reading the source of existing articles now” is a sign of a gap.

  This is the English version of the original Japanese article (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/aggregator-pagination/).

  More in English

- All English pages (https://koshinstudio.com/en/)

- Toreca Dash (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/)

# “Not just noticing; not letting it happen”: turning a report-only monitor into one that fills gaps on the spot

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/fill-the-gap/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-10-17
Development log of the Toreca Dash app / August 2026

  The goal of my app Toreca Dash is to show lottery information without missing any. The user’s instruction was: “don’t just notice; make sure missing things do not happen in the first place”.

  This article records how, on 27 August 2026, I turned monitoring from “find and report” into “find and fill on the spot”.

  Numbers come from my work log of 27 August 2026.

## A report-only monitor does not fill until a person notices

  The old gap monitor (reportCoverageGap) only reported. The gap stayed until someone noticed and ran a fix by hand. I made it create articles on the spot (fill), three times a day after the import.

- It uses the existing creation path. Duplicates are prevented by the existing check (hasExistingCoverageForStore).

- If the import side works correctly, this ends with 0. Anything created here means the import side still has a hole. Read the count as “the size of the holes left”.

## I added a log to the branch that silently dropped things

  An early return in one function (touchLastSeenIfExists) was the only branch that moved on without saying anything. All other branches log. That silence is why another hole (24 stores getting the same article ID) was not found for so long. A branch that silently drops is a hiding place for holes nobody can see.

## Even with no link, show “how to apply”

  Of 32 articles with an unknown application link, 17 were not given a URL in the other table either (a store’s app, an in-store QR and so on). But the other side writes the “how to apply” and “conditions” in prose. I imported those and passed them to the application-method detector. “Apply in the app” or “apply with the QR code in store” helps more than “we do not know where to apply”.

## Articles missed by the link repair

  Articles marked “application link unknown” that were neither app-only nor pointing to an aggregator never became a repair target: only 15 of 34 were. I made the mark itself the condition for being a target.

## The final numbers

     | Before | After

      Gap coverage (against one site, 24 items) | 92% | 100% (96% on the way)

      Displayed articles | 1,444 | 1,488 (+44)

      Articles with an application link | 97.4% | 97.8%

  But 100% is a number for one site. A gap survey against the X aggregates found 3 stores, but the stored text was cut at 500 characters, so that is a lower bound. I decided to measure again after X monitoring resumed.

## What I learned

> Connect the mechanism that notices to the one that fills.

- A report-only monitor does not fill until a person notices. Fill on the spot.

- The count filled is “the size of the holes left”. 0 is the goal.

- Add logs to branches that silently drop. One silent place hides a hole for a long time.

- Without a link you can still show how to apply. “Apply in the app” beats “unknown”.

- Decide repair targets by the mark itself. A combination of conditions leaves gaps.

- 100% is a number for what you measured. Call it a lower bound.

  This is the English version of the original Japanese article (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/fill-the-gap/).

  More in English

- All English pages (https://koshinstudio.com/en/)

- Toreca Dash (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/)

# The same report for the third time: a SwiftUI button responded only on its text, and my two earlier “fixes” did nothing

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/swiftui-hit-area/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-10-17
Development log of the Toreca Dash app / August 2026

  The application-record screen of my app Toreca Dash has “Won” and “Lost” buttons. A report came: “the buttons only respond on the text; hard to use”.

  This was the third time I got that report (20 July, 1 August and 27 August). I had thought I had fixed it twice. The code said “fix”. And yet it had never been fixed.

  Written from my work log of 27 August 2026.

## The first two fixes did not work

  The first two times I “added .contentShape” and “moved .buttonStyle(.plain)”. The real issue was the order of the modifiers, and I had not got the order right.

  SwiftUI’s Button("Won") { … } has a label that is only text. Adding .frame().padding().background() outside to make it look bigger still leaves only the text responding to taps. The visible size and the tappable area were different things.

## The fix: build the look inside a ButtonStyle

  If you build the button’s look inside a ButtonStyle (the mechanism that defines a button’s appearance), the result is exactly the tappable area. Build it inside, not outside. I created an ActionButtonStyle and replaced six places (Won, Lost, Applied, enter announcement date, and “Apply” in two filters).

## Two similar items the same day

  Other reports that day had the same root.

- “Let me switch status in the deadline calendar.” I made the badge I had added earlier switch between “Applied” and “Not yet” on tap. But the row itself was a Button, so a button inside it did not respond. I changed the row to a tap gesture (contentShape + onTapGesture). Also Won and Lost are not switched, since they are “records”: a mis-tap that erases one cannot be undone.

- “Mailed, yet it has a location.” An article for Rakuten Books (mail order only) had coordinates in Shizuoka. I had judged mail order only by the site prefix, so aggregator-derived articles (a different prefix) slipped through. I now judge by store name too. Another cause: even after switching it to delivery, I had not cleared the coordinates and prefecture. If the prefecture remains, area filtering stops the article showing to users in other prefectures (mailed, yet shown only to people in Shizuoka).

## What I learned

> Before writing “fixed”, search for the same shape elsewhere.

- When the same report comes twice, doubt the fix. Even if the code says “fix”, it may not work.

- Visible size and responsive area are different things. Building inside a ButtonStyle makes them match.

- Look for the same shape on every screen. grep every place that is written the same way and fix them.

- Make irreversible records safe from mis-taps. Only “Applied” switches.

- When you correct a value, correct its related values. If you change to delivery, clear coordinates and prefecture too.

  This is the English version of the original Japanese article (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/swiftui-hit-area/).

  More in English

- All English pages (https://koshinstudio.com/en/)

- Toreca Dash (https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/)

# “Weird articles keep multiplying”: I counted by creation route and closed the entrances, and my counting was wrong twice

  日本語版 (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/weird-articles-by-route/)

Written by Koshin (https://koshinstudio.com/en/about/#operator) (web engineer and app engineer) · published 2026-10-17
Development log of the Toreca Dash app / August 2026

  For my app Toreca Dash the instruction came: “weird articles keep multiplying. No deadlines, so many odd articles. Solve it permanently. Investigate the articles made by other routes thoroughly too.”

  This article records counting articles by the route that created them and closing the entrances, and also how I got the counting wrong twice.

  Numbers come from my work log of 28 August 2026.

## I counted by route

  Articles are created by several routes (stores’ official X posts, store sites, aggregator sites, AI discovery). I counted what kinds of “weird articles” each route had.

    Route | Lotteries | No deadline | Link is a search result | Link is a top page | Link is the aggregator itself

      X (store official) | 118 | 11 | 0 | 1 | 0

      Store site (direct) | 63 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0

      Aggregator A | 39 | 33 | 3 | 2 | 8

      Aggregator B | 28 | 11 | 0 | 1 | 5

      AI discovery | 4 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0

      Total | 252 | 58 | 4 | 4 | 13

## I corrected my counting twice

- First I counted over all articles and said “1,204 of 1,398 have no deadline (86%)”. A deadline is a concept only for lotteries. First-come sales (1,055) and reservations (91) never had one. I had counted without checking what the field means.

- I wrote “the saved chunk is another store’s (98%)”, but in fact the full post text was stored and it just happened to begin with Amazon. I asserted from the leading marker alone.

## Holes found and fixes

### 1. Ended rounds left in the aggregator’s table were imported every day (33)

  The aggregator keeps past rounds in its table. In real data, a store’s “13–14 July” was imported on 27 August; the deadline was in the past and not adopted, giving an article with an empty deadline. With no deadline, the mechanism that removes articles past their deadline never acts, and it stays forever.

  I closed the entrance in three layers:

- Read the acceptance period as a date and skip rows that have ended.

- If a deadline cannot be read, do not create the article.

- If the store’s row has ended, do not create it.

  Checked in practice: I cleared the mark, re-ran the import, read 24 stores and got 0 new.

### 2. The application link was not an application page (5 reports)

  A search-results page (?keywords=) or a site’s top page had been adopted. I added “looks like a search result URL” and “looks like a site top page URL” checks to the single gate that adopts application links. Every route goes through that one gate, so the fix works there alone.

### 3. The article holds the full post text, so a reader who forgets to cut reads the first store (39)

  The article’s source text (sourceText) now holds only that store’s chunk. The full text goes into a separate field for verification. Whatever the reader does, it cannot pick up another store’s value.

### 4. The deadline disagreed with the store’s own row (5 of 6)

  A deadline is looked for in “the text chunk, the page linked, the attached image”, in that order. But the last two are not necessarily that store’s information. In real data the saved deadline and the store’s row differed by 53, 18 and 20 days, each a finished lottery shown as open.

  I made a function that returns a value “only when an end is stated explicitly” and, at the end of fixing a deadline, a gate: if it disagrees with the row, trust the row. One caution: a function that also returns the date for a row that only has a start, like “from 19 June”, must not be used as is to overwrite.

## Clean-up starts with a dry run

- The job “hide articles with no deadline”: 33. Before running, I read each one’s own row period and confirmed all 33 had ended and 0 were open, then ran it.

- The job “align the deadline to the row”: 5. It does not hide; if the date has passed, the existing past-deadline mechanism removes it.

  Both repairs now run automatically every day at 4:20 and 4:30 (from 190 to 192 jobs).

## Result

     | Before | After

      Displayed lotteries | 252 | 199

      No deadline | 58 | 25

      Aggregator A with no deadline | 33 | 0

      Shown past the deadline | 5 | 0

      “Other site ended, mine open” | 12 | 7

  The remaining 7 are likely cases where mine has caught the newer round (the other table is out of date).

## What I learned

> Count by route, and doubt the counting itself.

- Count by route. A table shows where weird articles enter.

- Check what a field means before counting. A deadline is only for lotteries.

- Do not assert from a leading marker. The full text was stored.

- If no deadline can be read, do not create the article. Articles with an empty deadline stay forever.

- Make it impossible to pick up another store’s value. Do not rely on the reader’s care.

- If they disagree, trust that store’s row. The linked page and image are not necessarily that store’s information.

  This is the English version of the original Japanese article (https://koshinstudio.com/notes/weird-articles-by-route/).
